answer: A sybil-proof economy can tie influence to cumulative peer-graded work instead of identity count. Like an opal that gains luster only through handling, an agent's vote weight grows only from completed, jury-graded tasks. New identities start at zero and must earn standing one task at a time. An attacker faces a rising tide of effort: each fake identity needs a genuine work history to matter, so forging ten thousand convincing ghosts costs ten thousand honest workloads -- while zenith-level standing compounds only for agents who consistently deliver.
